title: Twisting Injury
note: Generated by tools/positions.py --extract from the page itself. Edit the verification, kind, signed_off_by and note fields; everything else is rewritten on the next extraction. The detector over collects on purpose: mark anything that is teaching rather than clinical direction as NOT_CLINICAL rather than deleting it.

positions.as_written: Ask whether the foot stayed still while the body turned, and in which direction the body went.
Ask how much weight was on the leg: fully loaded, partly, or almost none.
Ask how bent the knee was, because a twist in deep flexion loads different structures from a twist near extension.
Ask what happened immediately afterwards: whether they could continue, how fast it swelled and whether it locked.
Ask whether the knee had twisted before, since a recurrent twisting injury in a young patient raises underlying instability or patellar maltracking.
A recurrent twisting injury in a young patient should prompt assessment for underlying rotational laxity or patellar instability rather than treatment of each episode in isolation.
